description: Daily Binance USDT-M futures (BTCUSDT) metrics + USDJPY reference rate, for the dashboard's G6-feature/regime tile and JPY conversion -- collection only, not itself a trading signal.
source: metrics.csv: data.binance.vision public daily metrics dump for BTCUSDT (no API key, no geo-block, unlike api.binance.com), 5-minute rows averaged down to a daily mean. usdjpy.csv: ECB reference rate via frankfurter.app (free, no key). See scripts/fetch_binance_daily.py.
retention: kept indefinitely, appended forward. metrics.csv: first run backfills 30 days, later runs re-scan the same recent window and fetch only still-missing days (self-heals a day that failed due to a network blip or not-yet-published source file -- does not leave a permanent hole). usdjpy.csv: first run backfills full ECB history, later runs top up a recent window.

sum_open_interest.meaning: daily mean of Binance's 5-minute sumOpenInterest (BTCUSDT-M futures)

count_toptrader_long_short_ratio.meaning: daily mean of countTopTraderLongShortRatio (top-trader ACCOUNT count long/short ratio)

sum_toptrader_long_short_ratio.meaning: daily mean of sumTopTraderLongShortRatio (top-trader POSITION long/short ratio)
sum_toptrader_long_short_ratio.notes: distinct from count_toptrader_long_short_ratio -- one is by account count, the other by position size; do not conflate

count_long_short_ratio.meaning: daily mean of countLongShortRatio (all-account long/short ratio)

sum_taker_long_short_vol_ratio.meaning: daily mean of sumTakerLongShortVolRatio (taker buy/sell volume ratio)

date.tz: date as published by ECB reference rate (no intraday time component)

usdjpy.notes: ECB publishes one rate per business day; weekends/ECB holidays have no row (not a gap in the collection, a genuine non-publication day)

known_defects: metrics.csv values are DAILY MEANS of 5-minute source rows, not end-of-day snapshots or sums -- averaging a ratio series is lossy if the intraday distribution is skewed
usdjpy.csv has no row on days ECB does not publish (weekends, ECB holidays) -- treat those as calendar non-events, not missing data, when checking cadence
count_* vs sum_* prefixed long/short ratios measure different things (account count vs position-weighted) despite similar names -- see column notes above
